questions.stem: Why do the carbon anodes need to be replaced regularly during the extraction of aluminium?

options.text: The aluminium deposits on the anodes and blocks them
The cryolite dissolves the carbon anodes
The oxygen produced at the anode reacts with the hot carbon, burning it away
The anodes melt at the high temperatures used

questions.explanation: Oxygen gas is produced at the anode during aluminium extraction (2O²⁻ → O₂ + 4e⁻). At the high operating temperatures, this oxygen reacts with the carbon anodes: C + O₂ → CO₂. The anodes gradually burn away and must be replaced regularly, which adds to the cost of the process.

questions.stem: What is the correct half-equation for the reaction at the cathode during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: At the cathode (negative electrode), sodium ions (Na⁺) gain electrons to form sodium metal: Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na. This is reduction (gain of electrons). The chloride ions are discharged at the anode instead: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻.
